Cancelled by design: removal is a knowledge/connectivity boundary, not a global authorship-time cutoff. Facts accepted by a peer whose pinned snapshot still authorizes the sender are legitimate workspace history; informed peers eventually close sharing through grant expiry and exact Worker checks. No admission frontier is wanted.

Cancelled by design: inactive receipts are local durable intent, not a second replicated fact set. They may be published if a retaining node later reactivates them, but fresh replicas need not receive latent candidates and loss after every holder disappears is acceptable.

Cancelled by design: a removed offline replica need not learn a terminal tombstone. It may continue isolated local authorship; stale peers may legitimately accept it, while peers that know the removal refuse new grants and eventually stop further sharing.
